text:
anya: heads up — saw 3 OOMs on prod inference nodes around 03:12 UTC after the continuous-batcher tweak landed. all of them correlate with high-KV requests (long convo + big prompt). suspect batch admission isn't accounting for kv cache memory pressure properly.

mike: ah, saw an alert too. logs show batch formation allowed >8 requests with large KV footprints which pushed kv cache above the soft limit and then kernels started hitting cuda OOM.

shoaib: can we gate admission by estimated kv-resident-bytes per-request? we have telemetry that reports kv_live_bytes per-request from the runtime profiler. simple check: if sum(kv_bytes in queue) + kv_estimate(request) > kv_budget -> mark request as deferred.

rachel: agreed in principle. two quick concerns: 1) estimating kv_bytes for new requests (no prior traces) — we need a heuristic based on prompt tokens + model variant, 2) throughput impact if we get too conservative.

anya: for (1) we can use a linear model we already train in offline profiling: kv_bytes ≈ a * prompt_tokens + b * context_len_factor + c_model_scale. we have coefficients from nightly runs. for (2) start with a soft-admit policy: allow admission but cap total-kv-per-batch and if cap exceeded trim batch and mark remaining requests for immediate next batch. reduces cold defers.

mike: can you sketch the admission pseudocode?

shoaib: sure — quick draft:
```
# on batch attempt:
batch = collect_queue(window_ms)
sum_kv = sum(est_kv(req) for req in batch)
if sum_kv <= NODE_KV_BUDGET * SOFT_THRESHOLD:
    admit(batch)
else:
    # admission order = arrival, but drop from tail until under budget
    while sum_kv > NODE_KV_BUDGET * SOFT_THRESHOLD and batch:
        tail = batch.pop()
        sum_kv -= est_kv(tail)
        mark_deferred(tail)
    admit(batch)
```

rachel: looks good. two knobs to expose: SOFT_THRESHOLD (e.g., 0.75) and fallback timeout for deferred requests (e.g., push into next batch immediately).

lucy: also add a per-request kv_reserve tag for pinned KV-heavy calls (enterprise feature). those should bypass admission only if they have dedicated capacity. otherwise they get queued.

mike: profiling results I pulled last night: link: https://internal.redwood/profiles/17876-kv-batch-regressions — shows median est_kv per request jumped ~2.3x for long-convo cases. kernel selection seemed to favor single-stream kernels on smaller microbatches which increased memory pressure unexpectedly.

anya: that's worrying — kernel-choice + larger effective kv cache means we might need kernel-aware admission. i.e., account for kernel memory overhead per-batch when computing NODE_KV_BUDGET available.

shoaib: idea: add KERNEL_OVERHEAD estimate per model_variant and scale when batch has many short sequences (forces single-stream kernels). effective_budget = NODE_KV_BUDGET - KERNEL_OVERHEAD(batch).

rachel: and add a telemetry tag when we trim batches due to kv_budget, so we can track latency regressions per customer. we need a dashboard: "kv_admission_trims / minute" and "avg_defer_time".

anya: deployment plan proposal:
- quick patch to admission code to compute est_kv with existing linear model and soft-trim behavior (canary 10% nodes)
- emit telemetry for trims, avg kv per batch, kernel_overhead estimate
- after 48h of canary, tweak SOFT_THRESHOLD and fallback timeout based on observed defer rate and P95 latency
- if trims hurt latency, consider secondary path: partial kv-eviction (LRU) for best-effort batches (riskier)

mike: sounds good. would like to add a safety belt: if node free memory drops below EMERGENCY_THRESHOLD then we should force-bail batch formation entirely and let upstream fallback to smaller model variant.

shoaib: implemented EMERGENCY_THRESHOLD check already in the draft patch — it rejects new admissions and returns 503 with a retry-after. cheap and safe.

lucy: one more ask — add an opt-in flag at route-level so product teams can choose strict vs. soft admission behavior. helps enterprise customers with predictable SLAs.

infra-bot: deploy started: canary group "kv-admit-softtrim-v1" -> 2 nodes in us-west-2 at 04:05 UTC. CI: green.

anya: cool. i'll follow telemetry this morning and post a short summary. thanks all — let's reconvene if we see unexpected latency spikes or if trims exceed 5% of requests for the canary group. :thumbsup:
